title: Edinburgh vs Dublin: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Edinburgh for dramatic medieval history and scenic wow factor. Dublin for pub culture, live trad music, and the best social atmosphere in the British Isles. Do both with a 1.5h Ryanair flight.

categories.name: Visual Beauty
categories.summary: Edinburgh Castle on volcanic rock is one of Europe's most dramatic city views. Dublin is beautiful but different.

categories.name: Historic Sightseeing
categories.summary: Edinburgh Castle, Royal Mile, and Holyrood Palace vs Dublin's Trinity College and Kilmainham Gaol.

categories.name: Pub Culture
categories.summary: Dublin's Temple Bar and trad music sessions are unmatched. Edinburgh has great whisky bars but different energy.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Both mid-tier for Western Europe. Edinburgh £60-100/day vs Dublin €65-100/day. Edinburgh expensive in August Festival season.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Edinburgh has Loch Lomond, Stirling, Scottish Highlands. Both have great regional options.

categories.name: Solo Travel
categories.summary: Dublin locals talk to strangers in pubs — exceptional for solo travelers. Edinburgh is also welcoming.

faq.question: Is Edinburgh or Dublin better for a first-time visitor?
faq.answer: Edinburgh for scenery and history; Dublin for pub culture and social energy.

faq.question: How far apart are Edinburgh and Dublin?
faq.answer: 1.5h direct flight (Ryanair/Aer Lingus from ~£30-70). No direct train.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: Similar cost overall. Edinburgh triple-priced in August Festival season.
